title: LEGO Star Wars MTT drops to £96.99 - is the 31% discount worth it?
summary: Brick Fanatics has revisited 75435 Battle of Felucia Separatist MTT a year after launch, now that Amazon UK has cut the price by 31% to £96.99.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Star Wars set 75435 Battle of Felucia Separatist MTT, which launched roughly a year ago at £139.99 for 976 pieces, is currently discounted to £96.99 at Amazon UK - a 31% saving of around £43. Brick Fanatics has revisited the set to weigh up whether this brings it closer to the roughly 10p-per-piece value benchmark many collectors look for.

According to the review, the set's standout feature is its droid deployment mechanism: a single dial on the back opens the front hatch and lowers the droids out, then retracts them when turned the other way. The build is otherwise straightforward once that Technic core mechanism is complete, and the set includes an exclusive Commander Bly minifigure plus an updated Aayla Secura, alongside six B1 Battle Droids, a droid pilot and three new Commando Droids.

## Why it matters
For UK LEGO Star Wars collectors, this is a useful price checkpoint on a set that drew criticism for its original RRP. A near-10p-per-piece rate, plus an exclusive minifigure unlikely to reappear soon, could sway buyers who held off at launch.

## What to watch next
Watch Amazon UK and other retailers for further price movements on 75435, and keep an eye out for whether Commander Bly reappears in future LEGO Star Wars sets.

title: LEGO Ideas kaleidoscope hits 10,000 votes, joins next review wave
summary: A working LEGO kaleidoscope built from Assembly Square mirror pieces has passed 10,000 supporters, putting it in the running for the second LEGO Ideas review of 2026.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A fan-designed LEGO kaleidoscope called KaLEGOidoscope, created by Milan Sekiz, has reached the 10,000 supporter milestone on LEGO Ideas. That secures it a spot in the platform's second review of 2026, which now stands at 56 qualifying projects ahead of the 7 September deadline.

The build uses mirror elements from 10255 Assembly Square to recreate a genuine kaleidoscope effect, with an openable top for swapping translucent pieces and a drawer to store spares. It's finished with a stand styled after vintage scientific instruments.

Reaching 10,000 votes only means the project enters LEGO's official review process — it doesn't guarantee it becomes a real set. Recent Ideas successes 21370 E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial and 21372 La Catrina both followed this same path before launching as official sets.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is one of the few routes for fan creations to become genuine, boxed sets, so tracking which builds qualify gives collectors an early look at what might land on shelves next. A working kaleidoscope built from studs and mirror tiles is also a fun demonstration of how creative the LEGO building community can be with standard parts.

## What to watch next
Whether KaLEGOidoscope is chosen by LEGO after the review closes remains to be confirmed — until then, its selection as an official set is unconfirmed. More projects are expected to qualify before the September deadline, so watch for further updates on the growing shortlist.

title: LEGO Reveals 40975 Mini Hogwarts Castle – But the Minifigure Is Nothing New
summary: LEGO has revealed its microscale Hogwarts Castle set for August 2026, but the single included minifigure is a recycled Harry Potter design that's appeared in several previous sets.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has officially revealed 40975 Mini Hogwarts Castle, a microscale build of the iconic Harry Potter location set for release in August 2026. The set comes in at around 700 pieces and includes just one minifigure.

Despite hundreds of subtly different Harry Potter minifigure variants existing across the LEGO Harry Potter range, the figure included here isn't new. The figure is so common that it can currently be picked up on its own via BrickLink for as little as 71p.

For display-focused sets like this microscale castle, LEGO often puts the building experience front and centre rather than using an exclusive minifigure as the selling point. That's clearly the approach here – the build itself is doing the heavy lifting, not the figure. For collectors chasing minifigure variants, this is one to skip, but for fans of compact display models, the castle itself may still be worth a look.

More details on pricing and full piece count for 40975 Mini Hogwarts Castle are likely to follow closer to its August 2026 release.

title: New microscale LEGO Hogwarts set compared to its predecessors
summary: LEGO has revealed 40975 Mini Hogwarts Castle, its smallest Hogwarts model yet, and Brick Fanatics has compared it against the two other microscale versions already available.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has officially unveiled 40975 Mini Hogwarts Castle, set for release on 29 August. It's the third microscale take on Hogwarts, joining 76419 Hogwarts Castle and Grounds and the larger, older 71043 Hogwarts Castle.

According to Brick Fanatics, the new set costs £34.99, uses 700 pieces, and measures 14cm tall by 17cm wide - almost 2,000 fewer pieces than 76419, which costs £149.99, uses 2,660 pieces, and measures 21cm tall by 35cm wide. The premium 71043 Hogwarts Castle remains the biggest at 58cm tall, 69cm wide, and 6,020 pieces, priced at £409.99.

On minifigures, 40975 includes just one - Harry Potter on his broomstick - matching 76419's single inclusion (an exclusive golden Architect of Hogwarts statue). The largest set, 71043, offers far more characters with four minifigures of the Hogwarts founders plus 27 microfigures. Coverage of the Hogwarts grounds also varies between the three, with 71043 focusing on part of the castle despite its size, while 76419 stretches further across the wider site.

## Why it matters
This gives fans a genuinely tiered lineup of Hogwarts display options at very different price points and shelf footprints, making the Wizarding World range more accessible to builders who don't have space or budget for the flagship set. It's a useful comparison for anyone deciding which display piece suits their collection.

With 40975 launching on 29 August, expect further reviews and full piece-count/size breakdowns closer to release.

According to Brick Fanatics, LEGO Ideas fan designer Brent Waller — best known for 21108 Ghostbusters Ecto-1 and 21328 Seinfeld — has now had a third pitch approved, this time 21369 The X-Files. Speaking in a roundtable with fan media, Waller and LEGO Ideas Creative Lead Jordan Scott explained that because Waller has been through the approval process before, the team had to find new ways to keep the moment a surprise, since he was starting to recognise the signs of an approval call coming.

Waller also recalled how different each experience has been, working with different LEGO Ideas team members each time due to staff changes over the years.

The set is officially confirmed for release on 1 August 2026 for LEGO Insiders, with a wider release following on 4 August 2026.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas sets rely on genuine fan creativity reaching production, and repeat successes like Waller's show how the programme can turn passionate builders into recurring official contributors. For collectors, it's also a heads-up on a confirmed release date to plan around.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for full reveal details on 21369 The X-Files, including piece count and price, as the official launch date approaches.

title: LEGO Star Trek Bridge set: all eight new minifigures revealed
summary: Brick Fanatics has broken down the eight new crew minifigures included in the upcoming LEGO Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge set, due out on 1 September.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to Brick Fanatics, the second official LEGO Star Trek set, 11385 Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge, launches on 1 September with 1,701 pieces, priced at £159.99 / $199.99 / €179.99.

The set includes eight new minifigures based on the original series crew, each with their own uniform colour, printing and expressions. Confirmed characters detailed so far include:

- **James T. Kirk** – Captain, yellow shirt, two facial expressions
- **Spock** – First officer and science officer, blue uniform, new hair/ear element, alternate raised-eyebrow face
- **Nyota Uhura** – Communications officer, red uniform with leg printing, beehive hair, earpiece accessory
- **Hikaru Sulu** – Bridge officer, yellow shirt, single face print
- **Leonard McCoy** – Ship's doctor, blue shirt, uses an older LEGO hair piece

Brick Fanatics notes further crew minifigures are included in the set, though full details on all eight weren't fully covered in the excerpt available.

## Why it matters
This is only the second official LEGO Star Trek set, so minifigure design choices — like Spock's new pointed-ear element — could set the template for future Star Trek characters and sets. For collectors and fans of the franchise, seeing how LEGO Group translates iconic uniforms and expressions into minifigure form is a key part of the appeal.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for confirmation of the remaining three crew minifigures and any official images or announcements from LEGO Group ahead of the 1 September release.
